newsitem.title: UK: Euro vegetable oil closes higher on overseas gains.
newsitem.headline: Euro vegetable oil closes higher on overseas gains.

text.p: Firmer markets in Asia and the U.S. boosted closing European vegetable oil prices in quiet trading on Thursday.
Talk of increased exports of Malaysian palm oil during the first ten days of April underpinned palm oil.
Malaysian traders were estimating exports between April 1 and 10 at 203,000 to 206,000 tonnes.
The USDA's weekly export sales report showed soy oil exports at 7,900 tonnes, near the high end of U.S. trade expectations of between 5,000 and 10,0000 tonnes.
Crude palm oil cif Europe closed $2.50 up with no further business reported during the afternoon.

RBD palm oil also finished $2.50 higher while olein closed $2.50 to $7.50 up with additional trades reported for prompt at $582.50, dated May at $577.50 and Jul/Sep at $565 a tonne fob Malaysian ports.
Coconut oil closed around $5 up after Mar/Apr traded at $725, Apr/May at $717.50 and May/Jun at $712.50 a tonne cif Europe.
Trading in soft oil was light with only a few odd trade reported throughout the day.
Soy oil closed 1.25 guilders higher after May fetched 102.25 and 102.50 and Nov/Jan at 103 guilders.
Rapeoil finished 0.50 to 1.25 guilders higher after May/Jul traded at 103 and 103.75, Aug/Oct at 101 and 101.75 and Nov/Jan at 102.75 guilders a 100 kilos fob ex-mill.
Traders said news that Tunisia had bought 27,000 tonnes of soy oil for arrival between May and July had little impact.
